version/1.6.8
Description
tomgehrmann
opened
on Apr 5, 2025
Issue body actions
What happened?
When using a non-root user (and (probably WLOG) in my case user namespace remapping) with the container, notification plugins don't work.
crowdsec | time="2025-04-05T20:08:07Z" level=info msg="initiating plugin broker"
crowdsec | time="2025-04-05T20:08:07Z" level=fatal msg="api server init: unable to run plugin broker: while loading plugin: while getting current user: user: Current requires cgo or $USER set in environment"
If
USER=root
is set:
crowdsec | time="2025-04-05T20:05:12Z" level=info msg="initiating plugin broker"
crowdsec | time="2025-04-05T20:05:12Z" level=fatal msg="api server init: unable to run plugin broker: while loading plugin: plugin at /usr/local/lib/crowdsec/plugins/notification-email is not owned by user 'root'"
But it
is
always owned by
root
:
$
sudo docker
exec
crowdsec ls -l /usr/local/lib/crowdsec/plugins
total 156284
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26733528 Mar 25 15:58 notification-email
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26674488 Mar 25 15:58 notification-file
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26626296 Mar 25 15:58 notification-http
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26618040 Mar 25 15:58 notification-sentinel
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26753688 Mar 25 15:58 notification-slack
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 26618136 Mar 25 15:58 notification-splunk
According to the documentation, this should be sufficient:
CrowdSec rejects the plugins if one of the following is true:
plugin is not owned by the root user and root group.
plugin is world-writable.
This behavior is triggered when any notification is defined in
profiles.yaml(.local)
.
What did you expect to happen?
Notifications should work when executing the container as a non-root user.
How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
compose.yaml
:
services
:
crowdsec
:
image
:
crowdsecurity/crowdsec:latest
container_name
:
crowdsec
restart
:
unless-stopped
user
:
${CROWDSEC_UID:-1004}:${CROWDSEC_GID:-1004}
#
read_only: true
#
security_opt:
#
- apparmor=docker-crowdsec
#
- no-new-privileges
#
cap_drop:
#
- ALL
expose
: -
8080
#
http api for bouncers
-
6060
#
metrics endpoint for prometheus
-
7422
#
appsec waf endpoint
volumes
: -
./crowdsec/data:/var/lib/crowdsec/data
-
./crowdsec/etc:/etc/crowdsec
environment
: -
"
USER=root
"
#
or any other user (like ${CROWDSEC_UID}) (or comment out for first error message)
networks
: -
crowdsec-net
Consider the file permissions.
profiles.yaml.local
:
name
:
custom_default_ip_remediation
debug
:
true
filters
: -
Alert.Remediation == true && Alert.GetScope() == "Ip"
decisions
: -
type
:
ban
duration
:
4h
duration_expr
:
Sprintf('%dh', (GetDecisionsCount(Alert.GetValue()) + 1) * 4)
#
linearly increased duration
notifications
: -
email_default
#
or any other notification service
#
- ntfy
#
- slack_default # Set the webhook in /etc/crowdsec/notifications/slack.yaml before enabling this.
#
- splunk_default # Set the splunk url and token in /etc/crowdsec/notifications/splunk.yaml before enabling this.
#
- http_default # Set the required http parameters in /etc/crowdsec/notifications/http.yaml before enabling this.
#
- email_default # Set the required email parameters in /etc/crowdsec/notifications/email.yaml before enabling this.
on_success
:
break
A correctly configured notification service.
Anything else we need to know?
The information below is not from the minimal example above but from a more fully configured (failing) instance.
Notifications work if only remap is used (executed inside the container as root).
If notifications are not enabled and a non-root UID/GID is used, it appears to work correctly.
